questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Natural Resources' refers to.
questions.a: Natural resources are the gifts of nature that humans use to live and prosper - air, water, soil, forests, grasslands, fish, minerals and energy sources - taken straight from the environment rather than manufactured by people.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Natural Resources'.
questions.a: Anything useful drawn directly from nature counts as a natural resource.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Natural Resources' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1 (source: hees101.txt lines 1-90 (natural resources and their categories))

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Renewable and Non-Renewable Resources' refers to.
questions.a: Resources split by their ability to return: renewable resources like sunlight, wind, water and forests can regenerate within a human timescale if used carefully, while non-renewable resources like coal, petroleum and minerals take millions of years to form, so their stock only shrinks with use.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Renewable and Non-Renewable Resources'.
questions.a: Sunlight returns tomorrow; coal burned today is gone for good.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Renewable and Non-Renewable Resources' taught, and from which source text?
Explain in your own words what 'Distribution of Natural Resources' refers to.
questions.a: Nature has not shared its riches evenly: oil pools under West Asia, minerals lie in particular belts and rivers drain specific highlands, so different regions of India and the world hold different resources, shaping trade, settlements and even disputes like the sharing of Kaveri waters.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Distribution of Natural Resources'.
questions.a: Where a resource sits decides where industry grows and how regions trade.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Distribution of Natural Resources' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: 1 (source: hees101.txt lines 295-460 (distribution of natural resources, Kaveri dispute))

concepts.title: Responsible and Wise Use of Resources

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Responsible and Wise Use of Resources' refers to.
questions.a: Because resources are finite or slow to renew, wise use means the three R's - reduce what we consume, reuse what we can, recycle materials - along with conserving water and soil and shifting to renewable energy so future generations inherit working resources.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Responsible and Wise Use of Resources'.
questions.a: Reduce, reuse, recycle - sustainable habits keep resources alive for tomorrow.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Responsible and Wise Use of Resources' taught, and from which source text?
